facts.text: Presque Isle was named in 1828 after the French phrase meaning “almost an island,” reflecting its peninsular shape.
The 1912 fire station on Church Street now houses the Presque Isle Historical Society, preserving the town’s early civic life.
WUPI, the University of Maine at Presque Isle’s student radio station, broadcasts on 91.1 FM, a change from its original 92.1 frequency.
The 1953 film Island in the Sky used Presque Isle as its central filming location, showcasing the town’s rugged scenery.
In 1914, the Aroostook Farm was purchased and became Maine’s first Agricultural Experiment Station, advancing local farming research.
The Mark & Emily Turner Memorial Public Library, a cultural hub, displays art shows yearly and houses notable sculptures and paintings.
